beats.care: If you're in engineering college, IT giants are still hiring freshers, but slowly and only when projects come in. Skills and internships matter more.
beats.what: Wipro ended September with 2,36,328 employees, 6,716 fewer than in June, its biggest drop in recent quarters.
beats.why: Its big new contract wins fell 58.6% from the previous quarter, so it needs fewer people on projects.

cards.body: That's down from 14,000 the quarter before. TCS says it is hiring for demand.
cards.caption: Freshers TCS onboarded in July–September

cards.body: Wipro's net profit slipped 1.4% to ₹3,201 crore even as revenue rose to ₹24,753 crore. About 13.8% of its staff left in the past year.
Instead of hiring big batches every year and training them, companies now hire when a client deal needs people. Offers can come later, or not at all.
cards.title: what does 'hiring for demand' mean?

opts: It won far fewer big contracts
cards.q: Why did Wipro need fewer employees last quarter?
cards.why: IT firms staff projects; fewer big deals mean fewer people needed.

hook: Wipro *cut 6,716 jobs* in 3 months. Is campus hiring in trouble?

learn.t: Wipro plans about 7,500 fresher hires this year but had brought in only about 1,000 by the end of September.
